title: Finite compact Cech cohomology preserves existing coproducts
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space and let its open site admit sheafification of abelian presheaves [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Let $T$ be a finite type, $U$ an open, $(V_t\to U)_{t\in T}$ a family of opens, and $S$ a chosen Cech complex [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex] for this family. Assume each chosen intersection $S.W(p,a)$ is quasi-compact for every $p\geq0$ and tuple $a:T^{p+1}$. For any type $I$ and any family $F:\operatorname{Discrete}(I)\to\operatorname{Sh}(X,\mathrm{Ab})$ with an existing coproduct [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], the functor taking Cech cohomology in degree $p$ after forgetting to presheaves preserves the colimit of $F$, for every $p\geq0$. No injectivity hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 01FF, Cech-complex comparison; coproduct specialization via finite partial sums, using sheaves.tex Section 009E and algebra.tex Tag 00DB

proof.text: The coproduct sheaf is the sheafification of the pointwise direct sum. Every section on a compact open is locally a finite-support sum. A finite subcover gives a single finite union of supports. Coproduct projections to each summand produce global component sections; outside that finite union they vanish locally and hence globally. The sum of the finitely many global component sections equals the original section locally and hence globally. Conversely projections show injectivity. Thus evaluation at each compact chosen intersection preserves this existing coproduct, naturally in restriction maps. This argument does not require compact overlaps.

In degree p the Cech term is a product indexed by functions Fin(p+1) to T. That index type is finite, so direct sums commute with this product. The preceding identifications commute with restriction and hence the alternating differential. Thus the Cech complex of the coproduct is the degreewise direct sum of Cech complexes, with the original coprojection maps.

Direct sums of abelian groups are exact: write a direct sum as the directed colimit of the finite partial sums and apply exactness of filtered colimits. Applying this to kernels and images of the Cech differential identifies homology of the sum with the sum of homologies. These canonical identifications preserve the coprojection cocone. Empty covering families and empty coproducts are included.
